The publishing idea

Not simplified. Opened.

Rav Tzadok’s writing is compressed, layered, and allusive. These editions are designed to give the learner enough footing to stay with his own words.

Hebrew and English remain in close conversation. Sources and parallels sit where they are needed, so a difficult passage can be entered rather than merely summarized.

Resisei Layla

The hidden light of the Jewish soul.

Rav Tzadok HaKohen of Lublin explores Torah and prayer, faith and longing, and the light that can emerge from concealment. The two-volume edition presents vocalized Hebrew with close, phrase-by-phrase English and annotated sources.

How the editions read

A path into the original, not around it.

01
Original Hebrew retained

The learner stays attached to Rav Tzadok’s own language rather than being handed a detached summary.

02
Phrase-by-phrase English

The English follows the structure and movement of the Hebrew closely enough to help the reader move through the passage.

03
Sources where they matter

Talmudic, Midrashic, Zoharic, and parallel Rav Tzadok sources sit alongside the ideas they actually illuminate.
